title: The Missing Stone
intro: The Chronometer flickers awake. A shard of broken time has landed at Giza, where the Great Pyramid is being finished.

npcs.name: Merit
lines: You came out of thin air! Are you a messenger of the gods? No? Well, whoever you are, we need help.
This morning a polished casing stone vanished in a flash of light, and this strange glowing slab appeared in its place!
It keeps buzzing and running away from the workers. Could you catch it?

steps.text: Arrive at Giza around 2560 BCE.
Talk to Merit, the stone overseer, near the pyramid.
Catch the buzzing glowing slab (a smartphone!) near the workers.
steps.hint: Follow the radar. Get close and press E.

steps.text: Take the smartphone home to the Modern era. Press T to open the Chronometer, choose any year from 2008 to 2029, then return it from your Vault (Tab).
steps.hint: Any place on Earth works, as long as the year is right.

steps.text: The Chronometer has traced the missing pyramid stone to the Moon! Open the time travel screen and choose the Moon.
Find the pyramid casing stone on the Moon.
steps.hint: Jumps are high in low gravity!

steps.text: Bring the stone back to Giza around 2560 BCE and return it.
Tell Merit the stone is back.
lines: It's back! And it fits perfectly, look at it shine!
The pyramid will be finished on time. Thank you, Time Walker.

outro: The casing stone slides back into place. A ripple of golden light runs across the timeline.
mirra: [Signal fragment] …Time Walker? Is someone there? This is Mirra, of the Archive. I tried to hold every moment at once and the timeline shattered. Please, find the Rifts…
fact: The Great Pyramid was originally about 146 m tall and covered with smooth white limestone that reflected the sunlight.

title: Scrolls on the Wind
intro: In Alexandria, scholars are gathering the world's knowledge into one great library. But scrolls are slipping away through cracks in time.

npcs.name: Theon
lines: Welcome to Alexandria! Ships that dock here have their books copied for the Library.
Something terrible has happened! Three scrolls of geography vanished from my desk and reappeared all over the city, flickering like candle flames.
Could you find them before they fade away completely?

steps.text: Travel to Alexandria around 250 BCE.
Find Theon, the young librarian.
Collect 3 flickering scrolls around the city.
steps.hint: Use Q (Chronometer pulse) to reveal them.

steps.text: Visit the great Lighthouse on Pharos island. Theon says a scholar there can steady the scrolls.
Bring the scrolls back to Theon.

outro: Theon carefully rolls the scrolls onto the shelf. "Every book matters," he says.
mirra: …the Library. I loved it most of all. I wanted to keep it from ever being lost. I didn't understand that history must flow to be alive…
fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded under the Ptolemies in the 3rd century BCE, tried to collect a copy of every book in the known world.

title: The House of Wisdom
intro: In Baghdad, scholars from many lands translate and expand the knowledge of the world. An astrolabe has fallen out of time.

npcs.name: Yasmin
lines: Peace be with you! You are just in time.
Our master's astrolabe was knocked out of time. Its star plate flew off and the rings are scrambled.
If you find the star plate and align the rings, we can measure the stars again tonight.

steps.text: Travel to Baghdad around 830.
Meet Yasmin, the translator's apprentice.
Find the astrolabe's star plate somewhere in the city.
Align the astrolabe's rings (talk to Yasmin).
Return the star plate to Yasmin.

outro: The astrolabe clicks together. Yasmin smiles. "Tonight we will measure Aldebaran."
mirra: …in Baghdad they gathered books from Greece, Persia and India and built on them. Knowledge grows when it is shared. I see that now…
fact: In the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, scholars translated Greek, Persian and Indian works into Arabic and made new discoveries in mathematics and astronomy.

title: The Clock that Stopped
intro: In Kaifeng, capital of the Song dynasty, Su Song's great water-driven clock tower has stopped. Gears have scattered through time.

npcs.name: Lin
lines: Ah, a visitor! I'm sorry, I'm in a panic.
The great clock has stopped! Four bronze gears popped right out of the escapement and vanished into the city.
Without them the celestial globe won't turn, and the bells won't ring the hours.

steps.text: Travel to Kaifeng around 1092.
Find Lin near the clock tower.
Collect 4 bronze gears scattered around the city.
Go to Su Song's clock tower.
Fit the gears into the escapement (talk to Lin).
Watch the clock start again with Lin.
lines: Listen! The water wheel turns, the globe moves, and the drums are sounding the hour!
Su Song will be so relieved. Thank you!

outro: Water flows, the great wheel turns, and bells ring across Kaifeng.
mirra: …clocks. I thought if I stopped all the clocks, nothing would ever be lost. But a stopped clock tells no stories…
fact: Su Song's clock tower, finished in 1092, used a water wheel and an escapement to turn an armillary sphere and a celestial globe.

title: Stars of the Wayfinders
intro: Polynesian voyagers have crossed thousands of kilometres of ocean using the stars. But tonight, pieces of the sky have fallen to the shore.

npcs.name: Kaimana
lines: Aloha, traveller. You arrived without a canoe! That is a rare kind of voyage.
We read the rising and setting of stars, the swells and the birds to find our way.
But fallen star shards are scattered on the beach, and the sky feels wrong. Gather them so I can set them back in their houses.

steps.text: Travel to Hawaiʻi around 1150.
Meet Kaimana the wayfinder by the shore.
Gather 3 fallen star shards. They glow brighter at night.
Set the stars back into the star compass (talk to Kaimana).
Look at the sky with Kaimana.
lines: There. Hōkūleʻa, the star of gladness, is back where it belongs.
Now our canoes can find their way home.

outro: The stars settle into place, and the night sky glitters over the ocean.
mirra: …they crossed an ocean by reading the sky. They trusted the stars to keep moving. I tried to pin the stars still…
fact: Polynesian wayfinders kept a "star compass" in their minds. They read the rising and setting points of stars, along with ocean swells, winds and birds.

title: Gold, Salt and Books
intro: Timbuktu is a city of scholars, where manuscripts are worth more than gold. But time-wind is blowing their pages away, and something noisy has appeared in the library.

npcs.name: Fatoumata
lines: Welcome to Timbuktu! Salt comes from the north, gold from the south, and books from everywhere.
A gust of shimmering wind blew three pages of an astronomy manuscript across the city.
And there's a clacking metal machine in the reading room. It frightens the students!

steps.text: Travel to Timbuktu around 1340.
Talk to Fatoumata near the Djinguereber Mosque.
Sneak up on the clacking machine (a typewriter!) without being seen by its watcher.
steps.hint: Hold C to crouch and stay out of the watcher's view cone.

steps.text: Collect 3 manuscript pages.
Return the pages to Fatoumata.
Return the typewriter to the Industrial Age (1870 or later).

outro: The pages are bound back into their manuscript, safe in Timbuktu's libraries.
mirra: …libraries in sand and stone, cared for by families for centuries. They did not freeze their books. They copied, taught and passed them on…
fact: Families in Timbuktu protected manuscripts for centuries, and many survive today. They cover astronomy, mathematics, medicine, law and poetry.

title: The Knotted Cords
intro: High in the Andes, the Inca keep records on knotted cords called khipu. Some cords have come undone in time.

npcs.name: Kusi
lines: Allillanchu! Welcome to the mountain estate.
We record harvests and stores with knots on cords. Each colour and knot has a meaning.
Three cords slipped away, and now the storehouse counts are a mystery. Can you find them?

steps.text: Travel to Machu Picchu around 1460.
Meet Kusi, the khipu keeper.
Find 3 knotted cords among the terraces.
Take a photograph of Machu Picchu for your journal (P for camera mode).
Return the cords to Kusi.

outro: Kusi ties the cords back onto the main khipu. "Now the count is whole again."
mirra: …every knot was a memory, held by a person who cared. The Chronometer is getting stronger, Time Walker. It can reach the deep past now.
fact: Khipu, cords with knots, were used by the Inca to record numbers and other information.

title: Colours of the Ice Age
intro: In Ice Age France, artists are painting animals on cave walls. But a whirring machine is scaring the deer, and pigments have spilled out of time.

npcs.name: Ama
lines: You came over the ridge so quietly. Welcome to our fire.
I am painting the horses inside the cave, but my pigment pots have vanished. The red, the yellow and the black.
And a round, humming creature keeps chasing the deer away!

steps.text: Travel to Lascaux around 17,000 years ago.
Meet Ama near the cave.
Chase down the humming machine (a robot vacuum!).
Find the 3 pigment pots.
Give the pigments to Ama.
See the paintings inside the cave.
Send the robot vacuum home to the Modern era.

outro: By flickering lamplight, Ama paints a running horse. It looks alive.
mirra: …they painted animals that would outlive them by seventeen thousand years. Art is how a moment travels forward. I should have let them travel…
fact: Lascaux artists used mineral pigments: red and yellow ochre, and black from charcoal or manganese oxide.

title: The Iron Horse
intro: At Rainhill, steam locomotives are competing to run on the new Liverpool and Manchester Railway. One team's valves have gone missing.

npcs.name: Edith
lines: Mind the track! Oh, you're here to help? Splendid!
The trials start tomorrow and three brass valves have rattled away into another time, or so it seems.
Without them the boiler can't hold its steam.

steps.text: Travel to Rainhill in October 1829.
Find Edith by the railway.
Find 3 brass valves.
Bring the valves to Edith.
Watch the locomotive on the trial track.

outro: With a hiss and a roar, the locomotive puffs down the track, faster than a galloping horse.
mirra: …steam, speed, change. So much change. I was afraid of it. But look how it brought people together…
fact: At the Rainhill Trials in 1829, Robert Stephenson and George Stephenson's locomotive Rocket won the competition.

title: One Small Step
intro: July 1969: a Saturn V rocket waits to carry Apollo 11 to the Moon. A gadget from the future is zipping around the launch site.

npcs.name: Grace
lines: Hey! You shouldn't be out here. Wait, is that a badge? Never mind, we need all hands!
Something is zooming around the pad, a floating board humming like a hornet. It's confusing our radar.
Can you catch it before the launch?

steps.text: Travel to Cape Canaveral in 1969.
Find Grace near the launch pad.
Catch the hoverboard.
Take a photo of the Saturn V on the pad.
Return the hoverboard to the Near Future.
Tell Grace the radar is clear.
lines: All clear! T-minus counting… you're welcome to watch the launch.
"That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." People will remember those words forever.

outro: Engines thunder, and Apollo 11 climbs into the sky on a column of fire.
mirra: …they went to the Moon and looked back at the Earth, and saw it whole. Your Chronometer can now reach the deepest past, Time Walker…
fact: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface while Michael Collins orbited above.

title: Eggs Out of Time
intro: A baby Triceratops has appeared in medieval Japan! Its nest, 66 million years in the past, is missing eggs.

npcs.name: Mirra's Echo
lines: Time Walker, I am an echo of Mirra, sent ahead to watch over the nest.
The baby is lost in medieval Japan, and three eggs have rolled away across the floodplain.
Be careful. A Tyrannosaurus hunts here. If it charges, run, hide or jump into water.

steps.text: Travel to Kyoto, Japan, around 1100, where the baby Triceratops was seen.
Catch the baby Triceratops!
Travel to Hell Creek, Montana, about 66.5 million years ago.
Return the baby Triceratops to its home time.
Find Mirra's Echo by the nest.
Find 3 lost eggs. Watch out for the Tyrannosaurus!
Bring the eggs back to the nest.

outro: The baby Triceratops snuggles beside the eggs. Far away, a herd calls across the floodplain.
mirra: …sixty-six million years, and still the story continues. I am waiting for you at the Archive, Time Walker. In the year 2999.
fact: The Hell Creek Formation in Montana preserves fossils of Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops and Edmontosaurus from the last 2 million years of the Cretaceous.

title: The Archive of Anywhen
intro: The Archive of Anywhen, where the Chronometer was made. Mirra waits at its heart, among the last shards of the shattered timeline.

npcs.name: Mirra
lines: You came. You really came.
I loved history so much that I tried to hold every moment still, safe forever. And the timeline cracked like glass.
You have shown me that moments are not meant to be frozen. They are meant to be lived, shared and passed on.
The last memory shards are scattered around the Archive. Bring them to me, and together we will set time flowing again.

steps.text: Travel to the Archive of Anywhen, Alexandria, in 2999.
Meet Mirra at the Archive.
Gather 5 memory shards around the Archive.
Enter the light at the Archive's heart.
Weave the timeline back together (talk to Mirra).
Speak with Mirra one last time.
lines: Look. The timeline is whole again, every moment flowing into the next.
I will keep the Archive not as a prison of moments, but as a library open to all.
The Chronometer is yours, Time Walker. Anywhere, anywhen. Go and explore.

outro: Light floods out of the Archive and runs back through every era. The timeline is whole.
fact: Imagined: the Archive of Anywhen stands where the ancient Library of Alexandria once was, a promise that knowledge would never again be lost.
